# artisanvirt_node (Resource)

Approves an enrolled hypervisor and manages its maintenance mode. Hosts enroll themselves with an `artisanvirt_enrollment_token`; this resource then runs the host preflight and provisions the virtualization stack, waiting until the node is `ready` (or `degraded`).

By default destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state. Set `decommission_on_destroy` to stop and remove the agent and drop the node from inventory.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Approve every host that enrolled and is waiting for approval.
data "artisanvirt_nodes" "discovered" {
  state = "discovered"
}

resource "artisanvirt_node" "hv" {
  for_each = { for n in data.artisanvirt_nodes.discovered.nodes : n.name => n.id }

  node_id     = each.value
  maintenance = false

  # Remove the agent and drop the node from inventory on destroy.
  decommission_on_destroy = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node_id` (String) Id of the enrolled node (see the `artisanvirt_nodes` data source).

### Optional

- `decommission_on_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, decommission the host (remove the agent and drop it from inventory). The node must not be clustered or host VMs. Defaults to `false`.
- `force_decommission` (Boolean) When decommissioning an unreachable host, forget it without cleaning it.
- `maintenance` (Boolean) Put the node in maintenance mode. Defaults to `false`.
- `purge_stack_on_destroy` (Boolean) When decommissioning, also remove the KVM/libvirt/Pacemaker/DRBD packages.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Address the agent connects from.
- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster the node belongs to, if any.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `name` (String) Node name.
- `online` (Boolean) Whether the agent heartbeat is recent.
- `state` (String) Node state.
- `state_message` (String) Detail for the current state.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import artisanvirt_node.hv01 node-0123456789abcdef
```
